A small chat bubble sits bottom-right on every tab. It answers questions about Real and the site, does calculations, opens tabs and **changes the calculators' inputs for you** — and it knows what you've entered on every tab.

- **Answer** from Real's public docs (`docs.realapp.link`: cards, Rax, Karma, OTD, Pro, packs, Arena, changelog), this repo's research notes and the [site guide](SITE-GUIDE.md), citing the source link.
When the docs don't say, it says "not documented / estimate".
- **Calculate** with the site's own code: OTD payouts and payback, the rarity ladder, EV / Kelly, odds conversion and de-vig, Rateboard owed-Rax, plain arithmetic (never "in its head").
- **Fetch live data** the way the site does: upcoming games with consensus odds (Tab 9's data), the game schedule.
- **Act on the page:** "take me to the calendar", "set Tab 7 to Iconic, 90 days, NFL only, budget 50k", "half Kelly with a 2,000 bankroll".
It validates every value (enums, ranges, `50k` → 50,000), opens the tab if needed, applies the change, tells you what changed, and **Undo** (header button, or "undo") restores the previous values.
It cannot sign in, post/edit/remove Rateboard offers, spend anything or touch passwords.

- **Route feature requests to the developer:** when asked for something the site can't do (a new calculator, tab or data source), it says so, shows a drafted email and gives a `mailto:rax@vivaanshahani.com` link (the chat-only `request_feature` tool in `shared/agent/tools.ts` builds the subject/body and the fully-encoded link; `Markdown.tsx` only makes that exact address clickable).
It is not exposed on the MCP server.
- **Know your context:** every tab registers what it holds (inputs, selections, headline results such as the top cards or the best-EV board).
Tabs you opened earlier keep their last state; tabs you haven't opened since loading are summarised from what they saved in your browser.
The **Context** button shows exactly what it sees, plus an activity log of what you and it changed.

```
 browser                                        Cloudflare Pages Function  /api/chat            Workers AI
 ───────                                        ─────────────────────────                     ──────────
 bridge: tabs register summary + params ──▶  system prompt = rules + what's on screen
 chat widget sends history + context           + top-3 BM25 passages from the knowledge base ──▶ qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8
                                                loop (≤ 4 rounds): model → tool calls          (function calling)
   page tools run in the browser   ◀── navigate / get_page_state / set_params / run_action / undo
   server tools run at the edge    ──▶ search_docs, calculate, otd_*, ev_calc, odds_*, live_odds, schedule, …
```

- **Model:** `@cf/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8` on Workers AI (override with the `CHAT_MODEL` var; falls back once to `@cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` on a model error).
Qwen3 is switched between thinking and non-thinking with a `/no_think` suffix on the newest user turn — **not** `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`, which makes Workers AI skip its tool-call parser (calls come back as raw `<tool_call>` text; `normalise` also recovers those).
After the Cloudflare allowance the loop can fall through to other free providers — see below.
- **"Trained on Real" without training:** retrieval-augmented.
`npm run kb` fetches Real's public docs (`llms.txt` → each page as Markdown), adds this repo's `README.md` and `docs/*.md`, chunks them and writes a BM25 inverted index + per-document shards to `public/data/kb/` (committed).
No embeddings, so no neurons are spent on retrieval.
Re-run `npm run kb` when Real's docs or ours change.

- **Page tools:** `shared/agent/clientTools.ts` (schemas) → `src/agent/clientTools.ts` (execution) → `src/agent/bridge.ts` (validation against `src/agent/catalog.ts`, undo stack, activity log).
Each tab binds its state with `useAgentSurface` (`src/agent/surfaces/*`).
- **Safety:** the browser's history is re-sanitised server-side (no `system` messages, tool-call pairing checked, sizes capped); tool results and page state are labelled as data, not instructions; page tools are limited to harmless, undoable input changes; model output is rendered by a small React markdown renderer (no HTML injection; only https/same-site links).

Workers AI includes **10,000 neurons/day free**; on a Workers *Paid* plan anything above that bills at $0.011/1,000. `functions/_lib/budget.ts` therefore counts neurons itself (token usage × the published per-model rates, stored in KV under a per-UTC-day key) and stops calling the model at `AI_DAILY_NEURONS` (default **8,000**). A typical question is ~40 neurons per model call (≈ 200 calls/day), a multi-tool question 100–150. A Workers-AI "allocation used" error also marks the day as spent. Soft per-IP rate limit: 40 chat requests / 10 min.

When the allowance is gone (resets 00:00 UTC) or the model is unreachable, the widget switches to an **offline helper** (`src/agent/offline.ts`): no AI, but it still opens tabs, changes parameters from "set X to Y" phrasing, undoes, does arithmetic and answers questions by showing the best-matching docs passages (`/api/docs/search`).

`functions/_lib/providers.ts` speaks the OpenAI-compatible API of **Groq, Cerebras, OpenRouter and Google Gemini**. One model call walks this chain (`callModel` in `chatCore.ts`):

1. **The visitor's own key** (key icon in the chat header → provider + key). Kept in the browser's localStorage, sent per request in `X-AI-Provider` / `X-AI-Key` headers (same-origin only — CORS does not allow them cross-site), forwarded to Groq or Gemini and never stored or logged. It skips the shared neuron budget entirely. A rejected key shows an error in the chat (it does not silently fall back).
2. **Workers AI** while today's neurons last.
3. **Site fallbacks**: any provider whose key is set as a Pages secret, in the order Groq → Cerebras → OpenRouter → Gemini (Gemini last: its free tier may use prompts to improve Google's products). Each provider has several models; each model has its own free rate limit, and one that answers 429 is parked until its `Retry-After` (per isolate, no KV writes).

Only when all of those are exhausted does the widget go offline. Set the secrets with `npx wrangler pages secret put GROQ_API_KEY --project-name rax-super-suite` (also `CEREBRAS_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`); `PROVIDER_FALLBACKS=groq,gemini` (or `off`) narrows/reorders them. Free-tier limits and model names change — they are listed in one place, `PROVIDERS` in `providers.ts`. Gemini 3 models need their `thought_signature` echoed back on tool calls; it is carried in `ToolCall.extra_content` (and Google's documented bypass is used for history that came from another model).

Everything you enter stays in your browser (localStorage). When you send a message, the text, the conversation and the context shown in the **Context** panel go to Cloudflare Workers AI to produce the answer — or to Groq/Cerebras/OpenRouter/Gemini when the free Cloudflare allowance is spent, or to the provider whose key you added; nothing is stored server-side. The assistant never sees Rateboard passwords or sign-in tokens (no tab exposes them).

| Setting | Where | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[ai] binding = "AI"` | `wrangler.toml` | enabled |
| `CHAT_MODEL` | Pages var | `@cf/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8` |
| `GROQ_API_KEY`, `CEREBRAS_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Pages secrets | unset (fallback off) |
| `PROVIDER_FALLBACKS` | Pages var | all providers with a key; `off` disables |
| `AI_DAILY_NEURONS` | Pages var | `8000` |
| KV `CACHE` | `wrangler.toml` | already bound (budget counter) |
